oil.summary: A sharp reversal dominated crude markets Wednesday, with WTI shedding 3.26% to $91.50/bbl and heating oil cratering 7.17% to $4.5853/gal — the week's accumulated losses now stand at 10.66% and 12.56% respectively, unwinding much of September's geopolitical risk premium. The move lower comes despite an ongoing US-Iran conflict that has seen tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf neighbors' export shutdowns. The sell-off appears driven by a confluence of bearish fundamentals: the EIA reported a 3-million-barrel crude build for the week ending September 18, while Goldman Sachs flagged that elevated prices near $100 Brent are suppressing Chinese buying. A temporary US easing of Russia sanctions and new Senate legislation targeting both Russia and Iran add further uncertainty. Asian crude imports hitting post-war highs provides a partial demand offset, but the market's direction today is unambiguously supply-bearish.
drivers: EIA crude build of 3M barrels and distillate stocks 12% below average weighed on the complex, reinforcing near-term demand-supply imbalance concerns
Goldman Sachs: $100 Brent constraining Chinese crude purchases, capping upside; Asia imports hit highest since war began but failed to lift prices
US temporarily easing Russia oil sanctions to tame price surge alongside new Senate sanctions legislation creates conflicting geopolitical signals around supply

gas.summary: Henry Hub surged 6.07% on the day to $3.144/MMBtu, extending a strong weekly (+8.79%) and monthly (+13.05%) trend that suggests tightening US domestic supply dynamics, likely amplified by broader energy market volatility stemming from the Gulf conflict and its knock-on effects on LNG demand expectations. TTF was comparatively quiet, edging up just 0.78% to €73.915/MWh. On the supply side, TotalEnergies announced an investment decision on the Ima offshore gas field in Nigeria to boost Nigeria LNG output — a positive longer-term signal for global LNG supply, though not a near-term market mover. News flow for this sector was thin today; the Henry Hub price action is the primary story.
drivers: Henry Hub up 6.07% on the day, building on a strong monthly trend of +13.05%, pointing to tightening US domestic balances
TotalEnergies FID on Nigeria's Ima gas field to expand Nigeria LNG capacity — bullish for longer-term Atlantic Basin LNG supply
TTF relatively stable at €73.915/MWh; European gas market decoupling somewhat from the US move, with the weekly trend still negative (-5.27%)

power.summary: EU carbon allowances dipped modestly, -0.87% on the day to $81.725/EUA, though the instrument remains well-supported on both a weekly (+0.72%) and monthly (+4.11%) basis. TTF's slight uptick today (+0.78%) offers marginal upward cost pressure on gas-fired power generation, but the broader EUA market appears rangebound. Dedicated power and carbon headlines were sparse today. A carbon capture startup announced CO2 offtake deals with three unnamed US oil producers, noting that federal incentive cuts and regulatory uncertainty are pushing firms toward private commercial arrangements rather than government-supported schemes — a structural shift worth monitoring for US carbon market development. Geopolitical noise from UNGA (Trump tariff threats) and the India-US Russia sanctions dialogue remained peripheral to EUA pricing.
drivers: EUA slips 0.87% to $81.725 but monthly trend remains constructive at +4.11%; no single catalyst driving today's move
Carbon capture startup pivots to private CO2 deals with US oil producers amid federal incentive cuts, signalling structural shift in US voluntary carbon markets
TTF marginal daily gain (+0.78%) provides modest upward pressure on European gas-fired power costs; broader geopolitical headlines had limited direct EUA impact today
